BUDGET CUTS LOGAN FINNEY 2-12-19 READER TRT = 1:15 BUT FIRST, PROVOST JOHN WIN-SEC RECENTLY ANNOUNCED THAT THE UNIVERSITY IS MAKING FIVE MILLION DOLLARS IN BUDGET CUTS FOR THE NEXT FISCAL YEAR. THE ACADEMIC BUDGET IS BEING REDUCED BY 1.9 MILLION DOLLARS, WITH THE LARGEST CUTS COMING FROM THE COLLEGE OF EDUCATION, HEALTH AND HUMAN SERVICES AND THE COLLEGE OF NATURAL RESOURCES. CUTS TO THE NON-ACADEMIC BUDGET, INCLUDING ADMINISTRATION, WILL TOTAL AROUND 1.2 MILLION DOLLARS. IN EACH YEAR’S BUDGET, THE UNIVERSITY ESTIMATES THE AMOUNT OF REVENUE THAT WILL BE COLLECTED FROM STUDENT TUITION. FOR NINE OF THE PAST 10 YEARS, THAT INCOME HAS FALLEN SHORT OF PROJECTIONS. THESE NEAR-ANNUAL SHORTAGES OF 1 TO 2 MILLION DOLLARS HAVE TYPICALLY BEEN COVERED BY UNIVERSITY RESERVES, BUT THOSE RESERVES HAVE BEEN DEPLETED. THOUGH OVERALL ENROLLMENT NUMBERS HAVE STAYED RELATIVELY STABLE, AN INCREASING NUMBER OF STUDENTS ARE HIGH SCHOOLERS ENROLLED IN DUAL-CREDIT PROGRAMS. THESE STUDENTS PAY SMALL FEES FOR UNIVERSITY COURSES RATHER THAN PAYING FULL TUITION, WHICH ACCORDING TO WIN-SEC HAS LED TO A 15 MILLION DOLLAR DECLINE IN REVENUE FOR THE UNIVERSITY. AS PRESIDENTS OF THE STATE’S COMMUNITY COLLEGES TOLD THE LEGISLATURE EARLIER THIS YEAR, THE GROWING DUAL CREDIT PROGRAM IS DISRUPTING HIGHER EDUCATION ACROSS THE STATE. DUAL-CREDIT STUDENTS ARE DRIVING ENROLLMENT AT IDAHO’S COLLEGES, BUT PAY LESS FOR THER EDUCATION THAN DEGREE-SEEKING STUDENTS. AS FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF IDAHO, THE PROVOST’S PLAN TO AVOID FUTURE CUTS IS TO INCREASE ENROLLMENT. WITH A THREE PERCENT INCREASE IN ENROLLMENT EACH YEAR, WIN-SEC PREDICTS, THE BUDGET SHOULD BE STABLE IN TWO TO THREE YEARS. TITLE IX HUNTER DIEHL 2-12-19 TRT: 40 NEW SEXUAL MISCONDUCT POLICIES FOR THE UNIVERSITY OF IDAHO HAVE BECOME STRICTER IN THE WAKE OF ATHLETIC DIRECTOR ROB SPEAR’S TERMINATION. TITLE NINE COORDINATOR ERIN AGIDIUS (AG-ID-EE-US) SAID THIS CHANGE WAS MADE TO BRING THE UNIVERSITY UP TO CODE WITH THE STATE BOARD AND ROB SPEAR HAD LITTLE TO DO WITH IT. BITTERWOLF CELEBRATION NINA RYDALCH 2-12-19 FINNEY PKG TRT = :30 HUNDREDS OF PEOPLE GATHERED AT THE BRUCE PITMAN CENTER FRIDAY FOR A CELEBRATION OF LIFE FOR LONG-TIME UNIVERSITY OF IDAHO CHEMISTRY PROFESSOR THOMAS BITTERWOLF. BITTERWOLF, A NAVY VETERAN AND INVOLVED COMMUNITY MEMBER, DIED IN HIS ON-CAMPUS OFFICE JANUARY 30TH. COLLEGE OF SCIENCE DEAN GINGER CARNEY (CAR-KNEE) SAID BITTERWOLF, RECENTLY DIAGNOSED WITH CANCER, TOLD HIS FAMILY HOW HE WANTED TO BE SENT OFF. THAT IS, WITH DRINKING, JAZZ MUSIC, AND A MARDI GRAS THEMED CELEBRATION. BITTERWOLF IS SURVIVED BY HIS WIFE AND DAUGHTERS AND HIS CLASSES WILL BE TAKEN OVER BY OTHER CHEMISTRY FACULTY FOR THE SEMESTER.
